title: Escalation Insurance: sellable response-windows and rollback protection for top accounts
creator: Claire Huang
description:
Summary: Build an "escalation insurance" product offering that lets strategic customers buy time‑boxed response windows (eg. 1h, 4h, 24h) and purchase automatic rollback protection credits that guarantee an operational remediation path for high-risk roadmap requests. Goal: reduce churn risk for key accounts by offering a commercial SLA product that ties to our Roadmap Intake flow and automates fallbacks when commits introduce regressions.

Background & problem: Sales and AM teams report repeated requests from top customers for contractual guarantees around timeline and rollback for prioritized features. Engineering cannot promise full feature indemnity, but we can offer a bounded commercial product that: 1) commits priority response and playbook invocation during escalation windows, and 2) pre-allocates rollback/mitigation credits that trigger automated mitigation policies in the Console. This product sits between free intake lanes and full custom SLO contracts.

Scope & deliverables: design the SKU and contract language; implement Console controls to attach escalation insurance to an intake ticket; add billing SKU and usage meter; implement policy automation to: route requests to a dedicated triage queue, enable pre-configured rollback jobs (feature flags + infra snapshot), and consume rollback credits on use. Deliverables include PRD, UI mocks for Console intake flow, backend policy service endpoints, billing integration, and a 6‑customer pilot.

Acceptance criteria: 1) PM/Legal-approved product spec and T&Cs; 2) Console UI to toggle "Escalation Insurance" on intake with selectable windows and credit counts; 3) Billing events emitted to invoices (billing SKU attached); 4) Policy engine can trigger a rollback job and mark credits consumed; 5) Pilot run with 3+ top accounts, telemetry showing reduced escalations or mitigated customer complaints.

Out of scope: full enterprise SLO contracts, on‑prem only automation (pilot is hosted API + Dedicated customers), changes to pricing model outside of the new SKU.

Key tradeoffs discussed: 1) Pricing vs. abuse risk — decided to limit per‑account lease window and require AM approval for renewals; 2) Automation complexity — phased approach: start with orchestrated human-in-the-loop rollback playbooks, evolve to automated snapshot rollback if pilot succeeds; 3) Legal exposure — require opt-in consent and standard indemnity clause for feature regressions.

Success metrics (pilot): customer satisfaction NPS for pilot accounts > +10; 40% reduction in top-account escalations for covered tickets; 3 pilot customers convert to paid SKU within 90 days.

Implementation notes: backend needs new policy tag on intake objects, a small policy engine microservice to track windows and credits, integration hooks to rollout service and infra snapshots, and a billing connector to emit SKU usage. Minimal schema changes recommended to avoid long migrations.

Links: Confluence PRD (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/ESCALATION-INSURANCE; Mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EscalationMockups; Pilot dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/esc_insurance/pilot-overview
